newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ERA says uranium mill hit by 1-month delay.
newsitem.headline: ERA says uranium mill hit by 1-month delay.

text.p: Energy Resources of Australia Ltd (ERA) said on Thursday that rains and labour disputes have delayed by one month completion of an expansion of its Jabiluka uranium millling operations in the Northern Territory.
ERA also said cost under-estimation and project management difficulties pushed the final cost of the expansion to A$53 million from a previous estimate of A$38 million.
"However, early operating experience has indicated that the expanded mill should be capable of exceeding design throughput by up to seven percent," ERA said.
The expansion involves the addition of a third mill at the mine site to increase throughput by 50 percent.
Production from the Ranger deposit for the June quarter totalled 1,104.8 tonnes, three percent below the corresponding period last year.
Total production reached record levels for the year of 4,236.9 tonnes, 23 percent up on last year's figure, ERA said.
"Record production levels can be attributed largely to optimisation of the grinding and leach processes made possible by stage two of the plant automation project," ERA said.
Sales of Ranger and third party material for the quarter increased 18 percent to 2,502.3 tonnes, it said.
Total sales for the year rose 28 percent to a record 5,420.6 tonnes, ERA said.
ERA chief executive Phil Shirvington earlier this month said ERA's net profits in 1996/97 (July-June) would not match last's year's profit of A$40 million because of lower world uranium prices.
ERA is 68.4-percent owned by diversified resources group North Ltd.
About 60 percent of ERA's uranium is sold under long-term contracts to utilities in Asia and Europe. The rest is exposed to world spot prices.
